claims: The 2026 Masters Tournament is scheduled for April 9–12.
Rounds 1-2 early coverage is on Prime Video from 1–3 p.m. ET.
Rounds 1-2 main broadcast is on ESPN from 3–7:30 p.m. ET.
Rounds 1-2 main broadcast is on ESPN App from 3–7:30 p.m. ET.
Weekend rounds main broadcast is on CBS from 2 p.m.–7 p.m. ET.
Weekend rounds main broadcast is on Paramount+ from 2 p.m.–7 p.m. ET.
Featured Groups coverage on Thursday, April 9 and Friday, April 10 is from 9:15 a.m.–7:30 p.m. ET on Masters.com, Paramount+, and Prime Video.
Amen Corner coverage on Thursday, April 9 and Friday, April 10 is from 10:45 a.m.–6 p.m. ET on Masters.com, Paramount+, and Prime Video.
Holes 15 & 16 coverage on Thursday, April 9 and Friday, April 10 is from 11:45 a.m.–7 p.m. ET on Masters.com, Paramount+, and Prime Video.
Featured Groups coverage on Saturday, April 11 and Sunday, April 12 is from 10:15 a.m.–7 p.m. ET on Masters.com and Paramount+.
Amen Corner coverage on Saturday, April 11 and Sunday, April 12 is from 11:45 a.m.–6 p.m. ET on Masters.com and Paramount+.
Saturday, April 11 main broadcast is from 2 p.m.–7 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+.
Sunday, April 12 main broadcast is from 2 p.m.–7 p.m. ET on CBS and Paramount+.
On The Range has daily coverage on CBS Sports Network and Paramount+.
Masters.com provides free comprehensive streaming of all featured feeds and the main broadcast.
Login is required for some TV simulcasts on Masters.com.
Key coverage includes Featured Groups, Amen Corner, and holes 4, 5, 6, and 15 & 16.
Augusta National Chairman Fred Ridley announced that The Masters has partnered with Amazon Prime Video to expand coverage in 2026.
On The Range coverage on Friday is from 8:30-10:30 a.m. on Masters.com, Masters app, CBS Sports Digital, CBS Sports Network, and Paramount+
Prime Video provides exclusive early coverage of the first and second rounds starting at 1 p.m. ET on Thursday.
